title: Stanford Seminar - Generalized Reversible Computing and the Unconventional Computing Landscape
summary: A Stanford EE380 seminar by Michael P. Frank of Sandia National Laboratories on generalized reversible computing. It surveys unconventional computing approaches as transistor scaling nears its limits and energy efficiency stops improving.
why: HN commenters cite it as an informative talk from a leading researcher in reversible computing, mainly in threads on reversible computers and energy efficiency.

quote.text: his Stanford talk is extremely informative
